packet.prompt: Review native-head-bank5 + face2 source emotion implementation. Legacy banks1-4/face1 retain unchanged explicit registrations/capabilities; only bank5 complete own face2 author geometry from happy rest. No approval, auto-selection, mirroring, whole-face warp or borrower ROIs. Brow source glyphs have analytic whole-angle bounds and original matrix interpolation refinement, local mouth flat/frown curves + convex combinations, speech aperture activity-gated, own source/closed-mouth plate repair strip. Current original actor expression clock must drive face through cuts; physical body clock remains original. Canonical five-camera actor fixture explicitly supports emotion banks. Return JSON {findings:[{severity,file,location,problem,sourceEvidence,repair}],unverified:[]}, max4 concrete SOURCE defects only. Do not run tests/callbacks/schema geometry/fixtures/samplers/compiler/server/browser/API pipeline/audio/video. All geometry and artwork coordinates are declared candidates NOT validated; missing runtime evidence cannot be replaced with approval. Identify source logic/errors, old canonical regression, geometry proof gaps or missing interpolation. Do not infer correctness of pixels or coordinates. The raw own source drawings remain unchanged. Do not recommend relaxing gates. Runtime tests belong exclusively to human model.

findings.problem: The claimed convex-combination proof does not validate the generated combinations that runtime emotionMouth can produce. Validation checks flat, rest-top, and frown independently, but does not enumerate or bound simultaneous smile/frown weights, round deformation, aperture, or closure-related generated geometry.
findings.sourceEvidence: The validator loops over [f.mouth.top, emotion.mouth.flat, emotion.mouth.frown] and only tests aperture and round extremes. Runtime emotionMouth computes weighted combinations from all three bases and applies round shrinkage.
findings.repair: Validate the complete bounded interpolation domain used by emotionMouth, including mixed smile/frown weights and round/aperture extremes, or add an analytic hull proof covering every generated control point and ink stroke.

findings.problem: Lid interpolation error is measured at eye glyph vertices rather than at the registered lid curve and its stroke envelope. This can report a small or zero lid interpolation error while the actual interpolated lid geometry deviates outside its source region.
findings.sourceEvidence: The loop covers suffixes ['glyph','lid'], but for both suffixes it iterates `for(const p of f.eyes[side].glyph)`. The validator separately treats lid geometry and stroke as distinct geometry.
findings.repair: For the lid case, evaluate the lid curve control points and a conservative stroke hull; retain glyph vertices only for the glyph case. Include the brow glyph geometry in an equivalent interpolation proof where brow matrices are interpolated.

findings.problem: The own emotion repair source is emitted with opacity 0 and is only made visible through nativeHeadFaceState when `changed` is nonzero. At the declared happy rest emotion, changed is zero, so a face2 cell with no separate rest plate can leave the required own source/closed-mouth repair unavailable at rest, while the generated mouth is also hidden at zero aperture.
findings.sourceEvidence: `emotionRepair` is wrapped in `opacity="0"`; `nativeHeadFaceState` assigns `prefix+'-mouth-emotion-repair'` opacity `changed`, where `changed=ease(Math.min(1,1-emotion.smile+emotion.frown))`. NATIVE_FACE_REST_EMOTION has smile:1, frown:0, making changed zero.
findings.repair: Define and apply an explicit rest/closed-mouth repair state for face2, independent of reaction change weighting, while preserving the original happy-rest expression semantics and local-only repair gate.

findings.problem: The brow rotation proof bounds transformed glyph vertices but does not include the brow stroke or the transformed source strip artwork. The comment claims the rectangle is conservative for all generated brow ink, yet no stroke-width or sampled-strip envelope is included in the tested hull.
findings.sourceEvidence: The brow check computes extrema from `b.glyph` points and vertical up/down shifts only, then tests that rectangle against b.region. Brow stroke is not part of Brow geometry, and b.strip is checked only for crop/overlap, not transformed ink bounds.
findings.repair: Add an explicit bounded stroke envelope and transformed strip/source-art bounds to the analytic whole-angle proof, or represent and validate the required conservative source-art envelope without altering the raw drawings.

dispositions.reason: Normalized smile/frown weights are nonnegative and sum to one with flat, even if sum>1. For fixed round/aperture every mouth/teeth/tongue control is affine in the three base curves; round/aperture are multi-affine (product aperture*round). All 3*2*2 extrema were already validated in convex mask with fixed stroke pad. Eye closure changes no mouth control. Added explicit proof comments and deferred independent mixed-domain callback; no gate weakened.

Lid matrix is pure translation, so interpolation displacement is independent of the reference point. Original glyph-corner measurement is numerically the same displacement, not the claimed high-severity geometric defect. Code now explicitly measures the own lid control/stroke hull; brow own raster matrix refinement remains included.

Rest smile is already visible in Lila original source. Karo keeps the separate existing own closed-mouth plate at opacity1. New reaction repair must remain hidden at happy rest to preserve native paint. Making it visible unconditionally would repaint a correct source rest; no change applied. Deferred rest/silence checks assert the intended state.

Brow is clipped original raster ink, no generated SVG stroke. Transform hull bounds the actual source glyph clipping polygon. Skin strip is static inside that original glyph erase mask and never receives the brow transform. Added comments explicitly distinguishing raster ink, static erase sample and moving glyph; no speculative stroke field or widened masks.

scope: One bounded source-only review; source advice, not geometry/art/runtime/quality acceptance. No retries or automatic application.

postReviewParentFinding.problem: Face2 reaction repair opacity could leave native ink visible under the moving glyph, creating doubled contours during a reaction or blink/target change.
postReviewParentFinding.repair: Own face2 mouth/eye/brow painter switches are binary with discrete compiler set calls; native erase occurs before local replacement. Interpolation/refinement remains on local glyph matrices and paths. Speech uses own blank reaction strip before generated mouth; native happy rest stays unchanged. Generic opacity refinement skips only those explicit bank5 painter selectors. Face1 remains unchanged.
